prompt:
Extract and normalize the one contact record embedded in the user's note. Return one bare JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country, each a string or JSON null. No other text.

First identify the record block: contact label–value lines with variant labels and separators such as colon, equals, or tab, in any order. Use only those lines. Do not use surrounding prose, signatures, email domains, or company suffixes to infer missing fields. Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Treat absent values, empty values, and whole-value placeholders (-, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD; case-insensitive) as null.

Route the values before transforming them. Reserve the country line for country. Among the remaining values, route any value containing @ to email, regardless of label. Route a value to phone if, after removing leading tel: and a trailing extension, it contains at least seven digits and only digits, spaces, or + - ( ) . /. Extensions include ext. 12, ext 12, x12, #12, and extension 12 (the extension digits may vary). For name and company, use their labels except when the name-line value ends in a legal suffix and the company-line value does not: assign the name-line value to company and the company-line value to name, preserving any missing value as null.

Legal suffixes, matched at the end case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. For company, remove the trailing suffix and any comma immediately preceding it, trim, then uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word. For name, split at the first comma if present and put the part after it before the part before it. Remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof, with or without a dot, ignoring case. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics through recasing; never transliterate. For email, remove enclosing angle brackets and a mailto: prefix wherever the two wrappers are nested, and lowercase the entire address.

Resolve an explicit country to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 from an English, Swedish, or German country name or alpha-2 or alpha-3 code, ignoring case. Accept common aliases, including UK and Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA and U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, and Czech Republic → CZ.

For a phone, discard tel: and the extension. Check for + or 00 at the start, ignoring an opening parenthesis. If international, remove any literal (0) before stripping spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses; replace an initial 00 with +. Keep the written calling code even if it differs from the explicit country. If national, strip formatting, remove exactly one leading trunk zero if present, and prepend + and the explicit country's calling code; without a country, return null for a national phone. The result is E.164: + followed only by digits.

Only exception to missing values staying null: when country is absent, empty, or a placeholder and the phone is international, populate country from its calling code if that code uniquely identifies a country. Shared codes, including +1 and +7, leave country null without affecting the phone. Never override an explicit country. Before returning the object, check that no present value was lost because of label swaps or formatting.
